doctrine: Task-shaped operating points, not cheap/default/max ladders
Enumerate and explain; no silent auto-routing
Quota and API dollars are non-fungible
Missing evidence stays missing — never invent Grok quality curves

use_when: Status reports, recovery notes, short summaries
known_gaps: Moved claude-sonnet-5-5/low -> claude-haiku-5-5/medium on 2026-10-07 by rule 1 (cheapest tier whose evidence clears the bar). Same-snapshot AA rows (2026-10-07, grade B): Haiku 5.5 medium beats Sonnet 5.5 low on GDPval-AA (1277 vs 1179) and AA Briefcase (1372 vs 1272), is level on GDP.pdf (15.2% vs 16.0%), and costs $0.047 per task against $0.345.

Haiku 5.5 medium loses on closed-book recall: HLE without tools 33.8% vs 36.2%, AA-Omniscience 4.5 vs 19.4. Reports summarize context the lane is given, so recall does not decide this op. Escalate to implement.standard when the report needs facts that are not in that context.
Low effort does not clear the bar: Haiku 5.5 low trails Sonnet 5.5 low on GDPval-AA (1125 vs 1179) and Briefcase (1112 vs 1272), and saves only $0.02 per task over medium.
AA cost figures omit Haiku 5.5's 5x rate above 100k prompt tokens. At that rate ($0.50/$2.50 per MTok) it still costs a quarter of Sonnet 5.5 ($2/$10).
No local success-rate series for the recover task family. AA does not say whether its Haiku 5.5 runs used a pre-release deployment.

use_when: Normal implementation with tests or review path
known_gaps: Re-checked 2026-10-07: Opus 5.5 leads GPT-6.1 Sol on the independent coding boards: Vals Terminal-Bench 4.0 65.2% vs 55.1%, AA Terminal-Bench 4.0 at medium 52.5% vs 48.0%, AA SciCode at medium 59.3% vs 53.2%. Sonnet 5.5 medium (AA Terminal-Bench 4.0 29.8%) and Haiku 5.5 medium (15.2%) do not clear the bar. Moving this op to Codex would also break review.audit's different-vendor rule.

Independent boards mostly test at max effort; the medium-effort choice rests on Anthropic's own effort curves (grade C), where Opus 5.5 medium beats GPT-6 Astra medium on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (57.6% at $2.94 vs 53.9% at $6.15).
Derived with scripts/recommend_ops.py against op-requirements.json (DRAFT); rerun on each catalog release.

Anthropic's launch table: 39.2% vs 70.6%. Haiku 5.5 reaches Sonnet's medium score only at xhigh (29.3%), which needs an override reason.

use_when: Small, well-specified patches that a deterministic oracle accepts or rejects (tests, type check, build)
Codex quota or dollars are tight and many such tasks run
avoid_when: No automatic oracle, so a reviewer would have to judge the result
Long multi-step terminal or environment tasks
known_gaps: Added 2026-10-07 by rule 1. GPT-6 Luna is the newest GA model in Codex's cheapest tier: $0.10/$0.50 per MTok and 2.5/12.5 Codex credits, against $2/$10 and 50/250 for GPT-6.1 Sol.

The bar: the oracle catches failures (detection 0.95 in op-requirements.json), so a Luna attempt that fails costs its own price plus the $0.50 attempt overhead before escalation to implement.standard. With a $2 expected cost for the stronger arm, Luna-first is cheaper when Luna passes more than about one task in three. OpenAI's DeepSWE v1.1 curve (vendor, grade C) has Luna high at 59.3% for $0.084 per task, against GPT-6 Sol medium at 56.6% for $0.38.
High, not medium: on DeepSWE v1.1, Luna rises from 44.5% to 59.3% for $0.03 more per task, which lowers expected cost under the oracle gate.

Independent boards show where Luna fails: Terminal-Bench 4.0 at max is 13.6% on Vals and 16.4% on tbench.ai, against 55.1% and 58.2% for GPT-6.1 Sol, and AA has Luna high at 4.6%. Long terminal tasks are therefore in avoid_when.
No independent board measures Luna on bounded repository patches. A local eval with hidden tests would measure the pass rate against the one-in-three threshold.

use_when: Hard implementation where rework is costly
known_gaps: Re-checked 2026-10-07: at high effort Opus 5.5 still leads the AA Intelligence Index (53.6, against GPT-6 Astra 50.9 and GPT-6.1 Sol 50.2), and it leads Vals Terminal-Bench 4.0 (65.2%).

Vendor harnesses not cross-vendor comparable; independent support is vals.ai Terminal-Bench 4.0 (grade C: Opus 5.5 61.6% vs GPT-6 Astra 57.1%) and AA Intelligence Index v4.3.2 (grade B: 57.6 vs 52.7 at max)
Moves load from the Codex pool to the Claude pool; check clawmeter headroom before bulk use
Effort 'high' chosen from vendor curves: Terminal-Bench 4.0 high 64.2% at $3.88/task vs xhigh 66.4% at $7.35/task

use_when: Independent review of another agent's work
known_gaps: Re-checked 2026-10-07: at high effort, the op's setting, GPT-6.1 Sol ties GPT-6 Astra on the independent boards that report high: AA Intelligence Index 50.2 vs 50.9 ($0.32 vs $1.73 per task) and ARC-AGI-2 91.7% vs 92.1% ($0.135 vs $0.668 per task). At max, Astra leads by 1 to 4 points on AA's per-eval rows and the Vals Index (63.1% vs 61.2%), and the two tie on tbench.ai Terminal-Bench 4.0 (58.2%). Vals Terminal-Bench 4.0, which does not state effort, has Astra at 59.6% and GPT-6.1 Sol at 55.1%. Under the pack's cost model ($100 per missed defect, no detection), the 0.4-point ARC-AGI-2 gap at high is worth $0.40 per task, which is less than Astra's $0.53 extra cost per task. GPT-6.1 Sol high is therefore the strongest evidenced different-vendor arm for its cost. Astra stays available by explicit flag.
Different vendor from the Claude makers (implement.standard, implement.accuracy-first). Opus 5.5 scores higher on coding boards but would check its own vendor's work.
No independent benchmark measures audit recall; a seeded-defect local eval would decide between the tied models.
GPT-6 Luna is not a candidate: it scores 13.6% to 16.4% on independent Terminal-Bench 4.0 runs.
Re-checked 2026-10-07: at high effort Opus 5.5 leads the AA Intelligence Index (53.6, against 50.9 for GPT-6 Astra and 50.2 for GPT-6.1 Sol) and ARC-AGI-2 (93.3%, against 92.1% and 91.7%).

No benchmark measures design/synthesis advice directly; choice rests on Opus 5.5 dominating Sonnet 5, Opus 5 and Fable 5.1 on AA Intelligence Index v4.3.2 (grade B) and agentic-coding curves (vendor, grade C)
Claude-family advisor reviewing Claude-family implementers is not a cross-model check; escalate to review.audit for independence
